title: SB686 (2023 Regular): Relating to the possession of firearms in certain public areas.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Oregon) (gun-policy Stage 5, Oregon); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Oregon text (Introduced, official copy, https://olis.oregonlegislature.gov/liz/2023R1/Downloads/MeasureDocument/SB686/Introduced; sha256 9056a58ff2b4cb8997c906f0febc08d1627787995b7771a54b12922147badb3d)
provenance.note: Introduced version; no votes on file. SECTION 2 also reworks the Class A misdemeanor outcome for licensees under ORS 166.370 (1)(b), not quoted here because the quoted passage is mixed with existing text; the digest describes it. SECTION 4 (ORS 166.262) is a conforming change to the license-holder arrest exception.

operative_text:
SECTION 3 (ORS 166.377): (3) The governing body of a city, county, district as defined in ORS 198.010 or any other entity that falls within the definition of “municipal corporation” in ORS 297.405 may adopt a policy, ordinance or regulation providing that the affirmative defense described in ORS 166.370 (3)(g), concerning persons licensed to carry a concealed handgun under ORS 166.291 and 166.292, does not apply to the possession of firearms within buildings and on grounds adjacent to buildings owned or controlled by the governing body.
SECTION 3 (ORS 166.377): (4) A governing body that adopts a policy under this section shall: (a) Post a clearly visible sign, at all normal points of entry to the buildings and grounds subject to the policy described in subsection (3) of this section, indicating that the affirmative defense described in ORS 166.370 (3)(g) does not apply.
SECTION 2 (ORS 166.370): (a) Any person who intentionally possesses a loaded or unloaded firearm or any other instrument used as a dangerous weapon, while in or on a public building, shall upon conviction be guilty of a Class C felony.
